entries.name: Command Phase
entries.subtitle: Step 1 of every battle round

blocks.t: At the start of the **Command Phase**, you gain **1 Command Point (CP)** (the player who goes first in the battle round gains 1, the second player gains 2), and every unit on the battlefield **reduces its Battle-shock** level if it was shocked (it returns to a Normal condition, unless it has the Battle-shocked ability).
Any abilities that happen "at the start of the Command Phase" trigger here, then both players resolve any end-of-Command-Phase effects before moving to the Movement Phase.

entries.text: command phase step 1 of every battle round you gain 1 command point cp

entries.name: Movement Phase
entries.subtitle: Move, Advance, and Fall Back

blocks.t: Units can **Move** up to their Move (M) characteristic in inches. A unit can instead **Advance** — roll a d6 and add the result to its move (and may not shoot that turn unless an ability allows it). A unit that started its move within engagement range can only **Fall Back**, moving away from enemy models; it then cannot shoot or charge.

items: Move models one at a time; no model can end within Engagement Range of an enemy.
Models must maintain coherency (within 2" of another model in the unit).
Terrain: Infantry can cross Ruins freely but must stay within the footprint when moving through them.

entries.text: movement phase move advance and fall back units can move up to their move characteristic in inches

entries.name: Shooting Phase
entries.subtitle: The active player shoots

blocks.t: The active player selects a unit, then selects targets and resolves attacks. Each eligible weapon can fire once per turn. To hit, roll a number of d6 equal to the weapon's **Attacks (A)**; each die that equals or beats the shooter's **Ballistic Skill (BS)** hits (unmodified 6s always hit, unmodified 1s always miss).

For each hit, roll to **wound** comparing the weapon's **Strength (S)** to the target's **Toughness (T)**: equal S and T needs 4+, S greater than T needs 3+, S more than double T needs 2+, S lower needs 5+, S less than half needs 6+. The target then makes a **saving throw** with its **Save (Sv)**, modified by the weapon's **Armour Penetration (AP)**.

**Blast** weapons gain bonus attacks against units of 6+ models. **Torrent** weapons don't roll to hit — they hit automatically. A unit can only target units it has line of sight to and that are within range.

entries.text: shooting phase the active player shoots each weapon can fire once per turn roll to hit

entries.name: Charge Phase
entries.subtitle: Engaging the enemy

blocks.t: Declare a charge with a unit: roll **2d6** and move the unit up to that distance. To succeed the charging unit must end within **Engagement Range** (within 1" of an enemy model, or within 2" for monsters/vehicles with the relevant rule) of the target.

If the charge fails the unit doesn't move. If it succeeds, the target can fire **Overwatch** (only with the Fire Overwatch stratagem) before the charge, and both units are considered engaged for the rest of the phase.

entries.text: charge phase engaging the enemy declare a charge roll 2d6 and move the unit

entries.name: Fight Phase
entries.subtitle: Melee combat

blocks.t: Units that charged this turn fight **first** (in the order the active player chooses), then all other eligible units fight. A unit can fight if it's within **Engagement Range** of an enemy — it makes attacks with its melee weapons, rolling to hit against its **Weapon Skill (WS)** and resolving wounds and saves like shooting.

Models in a unit must be in base contact or within 2" of a model in base contact to attack — attacks are then made against models in engagement range. Each model can make its full profile of melee attacks each Fight phase it fights.

entries.text: fight phase melee combat units that charged this turn fight first

entries.name: Battle-shock Test
entries.subtitle: When half your squad is gone

blocks.t: After a unit suffers casualties, it must take a **Battle-shock test** in the Command Phase: roll a **d6**. If the result is **equal to or higher than** the unit's **Leadership (Ld)** characteristic, it passes. If it fails, the unit is **Battle-shocked** until the end of the next Command Phase.
Battle-shocked units have **Objective Control (OC) of 0**, can't use Stratagems, and can't Fall Back. They can still shoot and fight normally.

entries.text: battle shock test when half your squad is gone roll a d6 leadership

entries.name: Cover
entries.subtitle: Benefit of Cover

blocks.t: A unit has the **Benefit of Cover** while it's on or within a terrain feature and every model in the unit is either wholly within the feature or within 3" of it and in the open would not apply. Being in cover gives the unit's models a **+1 bonus to their Save** against ranged attacks (not against attacks with the Torrent or Blast keywords, or attacks that ignore cover).

items: **Heavy cover** — +1 to save and an additional benefit against attacks that would wound (in some missions: -1 to hit against the unit).

entries.text: cover benefit of cover a unit has the benefit of cover while it is on or within a terrain feature

entries.name: Objective Control (OC)
entries.subtitle: Holding objectives

blocks.t: Every unit has an **Objective Control (OC)** value (normally its current number of models for Battleline, 1 for most units, 5 for many Monsters/Vehicles). A player controls an objective marker if their units within range have a **higher total OC** than the opponent's.
Battle-shocked units count as OC 0, so a shocked unit holding an objective can lose it to any enemy model in range.

entries.text: objective control oc holding objectives every unit has an objective control value
